control.why_the_coverage_differs_and_why_it_does: The coverage carries a per-body `lineage` digest; the trust-ir text does not. Section 0.3a already records that the lineage digest moves with the SYSROOT BUILD, not with the compiler delta, and this driver compiles against laneREG/sysroot-v13 rather than whatever std lane18's stage1 carried. The EMITTED IR -- the thing every fixture is compared against -- is byte-identical in both its binary and its text form. A second, independent proof of the same claim is below.
control.second_proof: crystal_fixture_freshness.py on the control dump exits 0 with 'FRESH: no chained body's instructions have moved' -- at the fixtures' OWN rev, which is the rebaseline record's stated postcondition. Its --strict arm fails only on per-build lineage and numbering, as expected for a different sysroot build.
control.verdict: CONTROL PROVED ON THE EMITTED IR; not proved on the coverage digest, for a stated and previously recorded reason.

subject.clean_rev_note: the crystal/complete branch tip, i.e. this measurement includes the 2026-09-09 Arc-data-offset strengthening
subject.verdict: FRESH -- no chained body's instructions have moved

both_builds_failed_their_BINARY_targets_: scripts/trust_ir_build.sh runs `cargo build -p clean-kernel`, which builds the package's six bins as well as the lib. Three bins fail `error: the crate panic_abort does not have the panic strategy abort` -- the release profile is panic=abort and laneREG/sysroot-v13's panic_abort was not built for it. This happens AFTER the lib's trust-ir is emitted and published, it happens IDENTICALLY in the control and the subject, and it is a property of the sysroot rather than of either clean rev. Both dumps are complete: 21/21 fixtures resolve, all 19 chained def_paths are present. It is recorded rather than hidden because it means neither dump carries the axes.json trust_ir_build.sh writes only on success; the subject's was regenerated afterwards with the script's own command (scripts/trust_ir_axes.py measure --coverage ... --log ...).
what_this_DISCHARGES: laneREV's stated blocker: the recorded producer IS now reproducible on this machine, and the proof is byte-identical emitted IR rather than an argument about revisions.
The owed comparison itself: 21 committed fixtures vs a live dump at HEAD, from an attributable producer, with a null result.
what_this_does_NOT_do: It does not advance `covered_clean_rev` in data/crystal_freshness_scope.json, and the AMBER verdict NUMBERING-SCOPE therefore stands. scripts/crystal_chain_revalidation.py refuses to mint a superseding record against a rebaseline record for a different clean rev (crystal_chain_revalidation.py:293), by design: advancing the covered rev means REBASELINING the 21 fixtures onto this dump, which re-pins what every link-2a lane compares against and requires each binding. That is a review act and is left to the owner. The measurement it would rest on is now done and is a null.
It does not re-mint the A0 census: that needs an -O0 arm as well, which trust_ir_build.sh does not compile.

a0_census_at_head.what: A fresh A0 census at HEAD against the CORRECTED (two-clause) discharge table, which the 2026-08-27 records could not be: they pin discharge_table sha256 dc4dacc8..., and the table was restated to f896a780... when the Arc-data-offset clause was discharged.
a0_census_at_head.how_the_-O0_arm_was_obtained: trust_ir_build.sh compiles ONE arm, so the census's second flip log came from section 7(a2)'s own recipe run directly (cargo rustc --lib -- -Copt-level=0 -Cdebug-assertions=off). The -Cdebug-assertions=off is load-bearing and is spelled explicitly: cargo emits none for the release profile, so -Copt-level=0 alone silently turns them ON and deletes ~30 #[cfg(not(debug_assertions))] bodies including the deployed infer_type.
a0_census_at_head.the_O3_arm_was_re-run_lib-only_and_is_by: clean_kernel.trust-ir.txt, .bin and coverage.json from `cargo rustc --lib` are byte-identical to the `cargo build -p clean-kernel` dump the freshness comparison used. So the three failing BINARY targets provably had no effect on the lib's emitted IR -- measured, not argued.
a0_census_at_head.verdict: The R2 semantic completion verdict for the designated target SURVIVES the strengthening: 197 = 196 + level::Level::is_zero, exactly one body discharged semantically, verified by name, zero others -- the same shape the 2026-08-27 record recorded as 190 = 189 + is_zero, now at HEAD and against the two-clause table. The census validates the discharge table fail-closed in both directions, so it also re-proves that the restated table is neither wider nor narrower than the walk.
